new.story: An Australian 10 cents from 2008, the everyday silver coin with the superb lyrebird fanning its tail across the back — the bird that can mimic almost any sound it hears, drawn here feather by feather. The front carries Queen Elizabeth the Second in Ian Rank-Broadley's portrait, the one Australia used from the late 1990s until the Queen's death. The lyrebird design by Stuart Devlin has been on the 10 cents since decimal currency began in 1966. The collection already holds a 2006 strike of this same coin; this 2008 joins it as a second year.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Obverse: ELIZABETH II and AUSTRALIA around the Rank-Broadley portrait with the designer's IRB below the bust; the date sits at the bottom and reads 2008 when followed in legend order around the rim (the digits base to the rim, so they present reversed left-to-right in the photo — read digit by digit in an enlarged, contrast-enhanced crop). Reverse: big 10 over the fanned tail of the superb lyrebird. Matches the collection's existing AU.X.10-cents type (2006 strike, C295) exactly in portrait and design; the 1966 first-year type is a different portrait generation and is filed separately in the collection.
